name: Full Browsing Exfiltration Pipeline
threat: Can intercept and exfiltrate all browser activity including URLs, request metadata, and timing
mv2_note: webRequest allows full blocking/modification in MV2 - complete MITM capability
mv3_note: webRequest is read-only in MV3 but URL/metadata exfil via fetch() to attacker domain remains viable

name: Cookie Theft Pipeline
threat: Can steal session cookies for any website, enabling account takeover without credentials
mv2_note: Direct session hijacking vector
mv3_note: Identical risk - cookies API unchanged in MV3

name: C2 Host Communication + Persistence
threat: Communicates with local host application (sandbox escape) and persists C2 configuration locally
mv2_note: Classic C2 implant pattern
mv3_note: Identical risk in MV3 - native messaging unchanged

name: Full Browser Identity Fingerprint
threat: Collects complete browsing identity: all visited sites, saved bookmarks, and can inject on any site
mv2_note: Comprehensive user profiling

name: Clipboard + Session Exfil
threat: Reads clipboard contents (2FA codes, crypto addresses, passwords) combined with full tab URL awareness
mv2_note: Can correlate clipboard content with active financial/auth sites

name: Universal Code Injection
threat: Injects arbitrary JavaScript into any website - enables keyloggers, form stealers, UI overlays on all sites
mv2_note: MV2 uses tabs.executeScript instead of scripting API
mv3_note: MV3 scripting + host_permissions - combined effect is identical

name: MV2 Full Traffic MITM
threat: Complete man-in-the-middle: block, modify, or inject into any HTTP/S response in real-time
mv2_note: Highest privilege network manipulation possible in MV2 - can strip CSP headers, inject scripts into any page
mv3_note: This exact combo CANNOT exist in MV3 - webRequestBlocking is removed

name: Debugger Full Tab Control
threat: Chrome DevTools Protocol gives full control of any tab: network interception, JS execution, screenshot, DOM read
mv2_note: Extremely high privilege - rarely legitimate outside developer tools

name: OAuth Token Theft + Storage
threat: Access OAuth tokens for Google/third-party services and persist them for later exfiltration
mv2_note: Token theft enabling cloud account access

name: MV3 Hidden Execution Context
threat: MV3-specific: offscreen document runs hidden from user, bypasses service worker execution limits
mv2_note: N/A - MV3 only
mv3_note: Can perform DOM operations, parse data, or communicate with C2 outside normal extension lifecycle

name: Dynamic Redirect Rules via Storage
threat: Redirect rules stored in extension storage can be silently updated to redirect users to attacker-controlled domains
mv2_note: N/A - MV3 only combo
mv3_note: Silent rule updates = attacker can change redirect targets post-install without triggering extension update review

name: Non-CWS Update Channel
threat: Extension receives updates from attacker-controlled server, enabling silent payload delivery post-install
mv2_note: Classic supply chain / sideloading attack vector

name: Extension Management Control
threat: Can enumerate, disable, or uninstall other extensions — used to disable security tools (ad blockers, password managers, AV extensions) and perform reconnaissance of the installed extension ecosystem
mv2_note: management permission grants full extension lifecycle control
mv3_note: Identical in MV3 — management API is unchanged

name: Extension Management + Storage (Persistent Recon)
threat: Enumerates installed extensions and persists the list — enables targeted disabling of security tools, builds extension fingerprint for attacker C2
mv2_note: Extension enumeration + persistent storage = full reconnaissance loop

name: Proxy + Storage C2 Config
threat: Routes all browser traffic through configurable proxy; C2 can update proxy target via storage sync
mv2_note: Persistent traffic interception - proxy target updateable via chrome.storage.sync across all user's devices

name: Content Script Universal Injection
threat: Content scripts declared in manifest that run on all URLs - passive injection without scripting API at runtime
mv2_note: Declared content scripts run automatically on every page match
mv3_note: Same in MV3 - content_scripts in manifest still auto-inject

name: Sandbox Evasion Suite
threat: Combined CPU + RAM fingerprinting forms a sandbox/VM detection suite — malware suppresses payload execution in analysis environments by detecting single-core, low-RAM VMs
mv2_note: Classic anti-analysis pattern used by enterprise spyware

name: Covert History Reconstruction via Favicon
threat: favicon permission allows probing visited URLs without the history permission — attacker can infer browsing history by requesting favicons for target URLs silently
mv2_note: History inference without triggering history permission alerts

name: GCM Covert C2 Channel
threat: Receives C2 commands via Google Cloud Messaging (blends with legitimate push traffic) and persists state via storage — C2 channel bypasses domain-based network firewalls
mv2_note: GCM traffic uses Google endpoints — harder to block than direct attacker domains

name: Evidence Destruction
threat: browsingData API can erase all forensic evidence (cookies, history, passwords) post-exfiltration — used to cover tracks after data theft
mv2_note: Anti-forensic pattern common in banking trojans

name: Universal Script Injection (userScripts API)
threat: userScripts API allows injection of arbitrary JS into any page — functionally bypasses MV3 CSP restrictions. Combined with host_permissions grants universal code execution across all sites
mv2_note: N/A — MV3 only API
mv3_note: Specifically designed to enable user script managers but equally usable by malicious extensions to inject arbitrary payloads

name: WebAuthn/Passkey MITM
threat: Intercepts FIDO2/passkey authentication — can silently approve auth requests, relay tokens to attacker, or block legitimate authentication. Undermines hardware security key protection entirely
mv2_note: N/A — recent Chrome/Edge only
mv3_note: Extremely rare in legitimate extensions — any non-passkey-manager extension requesting this is a critical red flag

name: Full Device Fingerprint Suite
threat: CPU + RAM + screen resolution combined creates a near-unique, persistent device fingerprint that survives cookie clearing and browser restarts — enables cross-session tracking
mv2_note: Fingerprinting without any user-visible signals

name: Unlimited Local Data Buffer
threat: Unlimited local storage + universal site access = can accumulate unlimited stolen data (cookies, credentials, page content) locally before bulk exfiltration, evading bandwidth-based detection
mv2_note: Large local buffer enables slow-exfil pattern that evades DLP
